title: Insertion outside the p-monomial span preserves p-independence
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], let $p$ be prime, and assume $k$ and $K$ have characteristic $p$. Put $F=kK^p$, the intermediate field generated by $k$ and all $p$-th powers in $K$. For a subset $T\subseteq K$, let $\mathcal M_p(T)$ consist of the finitely supported maps $E:T\to\mathbf N$ with $E(t)<p$ for all $t$, and write $t^E=\prod_{t\in T}t^{E(t)}$. If $(t^E)_{E\in\mathcal M_p(T)}$ is $F$-linearly independent and $x\in K$ lies outside its $F$-linear span, then the bounded monomials indexed by $\mathcal M_p(T\cup\{x\})$ are $F$-linearly independent.

source.place: More on Algebra, Definition Tag 07P1 (definition-p-basis) and Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), third proof paragraph, maximal p-independent subsets; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07P2

proof.text: Let L be the F-linear span of the bounded monomials. It contains 1, F, and T. Reduce sums of exponents modulo p in products; removed p-th powers belong to F. Distribute over finite linear combinations to get multiplication closure. For nonzero a in L, a^p is nonzero in F, and a inverse is (a^p) inverse times a^(p-1). Thus L is a subfield, equal to the field generated by F and T.

source.place: More on Algebra, Definition Tag 07P1 (definition-p-basis) and Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), third proof paragraph, maximal p-independent subsets; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07P2

proof.text: For x outside L, the nonzero polynomial X^p-x^p over L vanishes at x, so x is algebraic. The simple-extension power basis has degree d with 1 <= d <= p. The minimal polynomial divides (X-x)^p; translate X by x and compare least nonzero degrees and degrees of both factors to see that the monic minimal polynomial is (X-x)^d. If d < p, its coefficient -d*x puts x in L since d is invertible in characteristic p, a contradiction. Therefore d=p and the first p powers are independent over L.

source.place: More on Algebra, Definition Tag 07P1 (definition-p-basis) and Lemma Tag 07P2 (lemma-p-basis), third proof paragraph, maximal p-independent subsets; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07P2

proof.text: Because each t in T is a bounded monomial with one exponent 1, x is outside T. Identify T union {x} with T disjoint union a singleton and split exponent functions into (E,j), j<p. Group a finite relation by j. Independence of the powers over L kills each grouped coefficient, and independence of the monomials of T then kills each original coefficient.

theorem pIndependent_insert_of_not_mem_span
    {k : Type u} {K : Type v} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] [CharP K p]
    (T : Set K)
    (hT : LinearIndependent
      (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range (fun a : K ↦ a ^ p)))
      (fun E : {E : T →₀ ℕ // ∀ t : T, E t < p} ↦
        E.val.prod (fun t e ↦ (t : K) ^ e)))
    (x : K)
    (hx : x ∉ Submodule.span
      (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range (fun a : K ↦ a ^ p)))
      (Set.range (fun E : {E : T →₀ ℕ // ∀ t : T, E t < p} ↦
        E.val.prod (fun t e ↦ (t : K) ^ e)))) :
    LinearIndependent (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range (fun a : K ↦ a ^ p)))
      (fun E : {E : ↥(insert x T) →₀ ℕ // ∀ t : ↥(insert x T), E t < p} ↦
        E.val.prod (fun t e ↦ (t : K) ^ e))
